newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian committee recommends budget rejection.
newsitem.headline: Russian committee recommends budget rejection.

text.p: The Budget Committee of the State Duma lower house of parliament will recommend to the house that it should again reject the 1997 budget, Interfax news agency said on Monday.
It quoted the head of the committee, Mikhail Zadornov, as saying that members of the committee were unhappy with the new draft which had not been significantly changed from the earlier version.
The committee's recommendation is not binding, and in practice the fate of the budget will be decided by the Communist Party and its allies, who control 221 of the Duma's 450 votes.
The final timetable for further proceedings will be decided by the Duma's agenda-setting council on Tuesday morning.
According to a preliminary timetable, the Duma will discuss related tax legislation on Wednesday.
Under this timetable, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will address the house on Friday, and the Duma would then give the budget a first reading.
The Duma rejected the original draft budget in October with deputies criticising it for unrealistic revenue projections and inadequate spending.
The government and parliament then set up a reconciliation commission, which in November agreed a new draft to be debated by the Duma.
The new draft calls for a deficit of 95.40 trillion roubles, or 3.5 percent of gross domestic product.
